theme: Present Perfect vs Present Perfect Continuous
rule_en: Present perfect (have/has done) = a completed result or 'how many'. Present perfect continuous (have/has been doing) = an ongoing or recent activity, or 'how long'.
rule_bn: ফলাফল বা সংখ্যা বোঝালে present perfect; কত সময় ধরে চলছে বোঝালে present perfect continuous।

sessions.title: Spot the Error
sessions.instruction_en: Tap the wrong word, then choose the fix.

items.prompt_en: I have been fixing three bugs in the deployment pipeline today
items.explain_en: A countable result ('three bugs') needs present perfect 'have fixed', not the continuous.

items.prompt_en: She has worked on this Apex class since this morning so she looks tired
items.explain_en: An ongoing activity over a duration ('since this morning') with a visible effect needs the continuous 'has been working'.

items.prompt_en: How long have you deployed to production without a single rollback
items.explain_en: 'How long' asks about a continuing situation, so use the continuous 'have you been deploying'.

items.prompt_en: We have been releasing the new feature so the client can test it now
items.explain_en: A completed result that lets the client test now needs present perfect 'have released', not the continuous.

items.prompt_en: My eyes hurt because I have stared at the screen for six hours
items.explain_en: A recent ongoing activity explaining a present effect ('eyes hurt') needs the continuous 'have been staring'.

items.prompt_en: He has been writing four blog posts about Salesforce flows this month
items.explain_en: A finished number of results ('four blog posts') needs present perfect 'has written', not the continuous.

items.prompt_en: They have studied for the certification all weekend and still feel unprepared
items.explain_en: A continuous effort over a duration ('all weekend') uses the continuous 'have been studying'.

items.prompt_en: Our team has already been finishing the sprint so we can plan the next release
items.explain_en: A completed result with 'already' takes present perfect 'has finished', not the continuous.

items.prompt_en: I have been reading that documentation twice but it still confuses me
items.explain_en: 'Twice' counts completed actions, so use present perfect 'have read', not the continuous.

items.prompt_en: It has rained all afternoon so the streets are completely flooded now
items.explain_en: An ongoing activity over a duration ('all afternoon') with a present result uses the continuous 'has been raining'.

sessions.title: Choose & Fill
sessions.instruction_en: Tap the correct option or chip.

items.prompt_en: I ___ the deployment, so the new feature is now live.
items.explain_en: A completed result (it's live now) takes present perfect, not the continuous.

items.prompt_en: She ___ on the Salesforce integration all morning and looks exhausted.
items.explain_en: An ongoing activity over a duration ('all morning') uses present perfect continuous.

items.prompt_en: How many bugs ___ this sprint?
items.explain_en: 'How many' asks for a counted result, so present perfect is correct.

items.prompt_en: How long ___ on the Salesforce integration without a break?
items.explain_en: 'How long' about an ongoing activity uses present perfect continuous.

items.prompt_en: My eyes hurt because I ___ at the screen for hours.
items.explain_en: A recent activity explaining a present effect uses present perfect continuous.

items.prompt_en: Don't merge yet — I ___ the code review.
items.explain_en: An incomplete result up to now takes present perfect, not the continuous.

items.prompt_en: I'm tired because I ___ all day without a break.
items.explain_en: An ongoing activity ('all day') causing a present state uses present perfect continuous.

items.prompt_en: We ___ three new engineers this year.
items.explain_en: A counted, completed result ('three') takes present perfect.

items.prompt_en: She ___ for the certification exam since January.
items.explain_en: An ongoing action over a period ('since January') uses present perfect continuous.

items.prompt_en: I ___ that error before, so I know the fix.
items.explain_en: A completed experience with present relevance takes present perfect; 'see' is not used in the continuous here.

sessions.title: Build It
sessions.instruction_en: Tap the tiles in the right order. For speak items, say it out loud.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: I have deployed the new Apex class to production .
items.explain_en: Present perfect (have deployed) = a completed result: the deployment is done.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: I have been debugging this trigger all morning .
items.explain_en: Present perfect continuous (have been debugging) = an ongoing activity over a duration.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: She has fixed three bugs today .
items.explain_en: Present perfect (has fixed) with 'how many' (three bugs) = completed, countable results.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: How long have you been learning Salesforce ?
items.explain_en: Present perfect continuous answers 'how long' = duration of an ongoing activity.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: We have been working on the integration since Monday .
items.explain_en: Present perfect continuous with 'since Monday' = an activity continuing up to now.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: He has written fifty unit tests this week .
items.explain_en: Present perfect (has written) with a number = completed results, focus on quantity.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: My eyes are tired because I have been staring at code for hours .
items.explain_en: Present perfect continuous explains a present result through a recent ongoing activity.

items.prompt_en: Build the sentence.
items.answer: I have already sent you the report .
items.explain_en: Present perfect (have sent) with 'already' = a finished action with a present result.

items.prompt_en: Say a sentence with present perfect continuous about how long you have been doing your current task.
items.model_en: I have been reviewing pull requests for the last two hours.

items.prompt_en: Say a sentence with present perfect about a completed result you achieved at work today.
items.model_en: I have finished the bug fix and pushed it to the repository.
